Angular 21 vs Angular 22: What Actually Changed (And Is It Worth Upgrading?)
Press enter or click to view image in full size

Created by AuthorAngular releases have become more frequent over the past few years. Instead of introducing huge breaking changes every time, the Angular team has been focused on improving performance, simplifying development, and making the framework more predictable.
Non Members-Read Here
That’s exactly what Angular 22 is.
If you’re expecting a revolutionary release, you’ll probably be disappointed. But if you’ve been building Angular applications for a while, you’ll notice that Angular 22 continues pushing developers toward cleaner patterns and a more modern architecture.
Here’s what actually changed between Angular 21 and Angular 22.
Angular 22 in One Sentence
Angular 22 doesn’t try to reinvent Angular — it reinforces the direction the framework has been moving toward for the last few releases.
That direction is simple:

• Signals-first state management

• Less reliance on Zone.js

• Cleaner template syntax

• Better rendering performance
